subject.title: Rowland Unified School District Board, Area 3

text: Occupation: Teacher

strong: Educator. Parent. Rowland Unified graduate. Lifelong Rowland Heights/La Puente resident.

text: My name is Jeannette C. Alvarado, and I am running for the Rowland Unified School District Board of Education, Trustee Area 3. As a graduate of Rowland Unified, the parent of two Rowland Unified elementary students, and an educator with 15 years of experience, I understand the strengths, opportunities, and challenges facing our schools.

I attended Killian Elementary School, Alvarado Intermediate School, and graduated from John A. Rowland High School in 2003. The education I received, along with the support of my family, teachers, and community, inspired my lifelong commitment to public education and service. I am dedicated to ensuring every student has access to the same opportunities to learn, grow, and succeed.

Throughout my career, I have served as a classroom teacher, instructional leader, program coordinator, and union representative. These experiences have provided me with expertise in curriculum and instructional improvement, educational program development, collaborative leadership, and student advocacy. I have worked to strengthen literacy and mathematics instruction, support College and Career readiness through Career Technical Education (CTE) Pathways and Project-Based Learning, and improve outcomes for English Learners, students with disabilities, and other diverse learners. My experience has reinforced the importance of responsible governance, fiscal accountability, and data-informed decision-making.

As a Board member, I will advocate for policies that put students first. My priorities include expanding access to social-emotional and mental health supports, promoting responsible and balanced use of technology to strengthen teaching and learning, and using state, district, and school data to identify student needs and improve academic outcomes. I believe every student deserves a safe, inclusive, and academically rigorous learning environment where they can reach their full potential.

Strong schools are built through partnerships with families, educators, and the community. I will promote transparent communication, meaningful parent engagement, and collaborative decision-making while advocating for safe, well-maintained campuses, adequate staffing, and responsible stewardship of district resources.

As a lifelong member of this community, a Rowland Unified graduate, a parent, and an educator, I am committed to serving with integrity, accountability, and respect. It would be an honor to serve the families of Trustee Area 3 and the Rowland Unified School District, working collaboratively to ensure every student receives the high-quality education they deserve.

text: I've been going to RUSD school board meetings since I was 14 years old, and now I think it's time for a change. My name is Brandon Macias, I'm a proud community council member for Rowland Heights and the school site council president of Nogales High. As a product of our schools, and after years of serving as an educational advocate, a classroom aide at Northam Elementary in Rowland Unified, and a community organizer in Rowland Heights and La Puente, I've seen how a student's background determines their outcome. I'm running to build an educational system that works for every student, regardless of language, income, or documentation.

In an unincorporated community with no mayor or city council, school board members need to be more than just bureaucrats. We need leaders capable of connecting with people and affecting real change through tangible proposals. Most importantly, we need a government that delivers. So whether it's a pot hole in your street, or a concern in the classroom, I believe in a board where every issue that is yours should be ours.

That's why I've spent the last few years fighting against developers, fighting for the movement against AI data centers across the SGV. I believe government belongs to people, not to corporate profits or big money that doesn't care about our schools, or students, or our families.

That's why I'm putting forward a concrete plan that tackles the key issues in the everyday lives of our students and families.
My plan does this by: putting aides at each of our elementary schools tackling issues of literacy and math intervention, using our in-house transportation department to add additional bus routes for student pickup and drop-off to support working families, and working with local organizations to provide free legal aid in addition to strengthening policy against the collection of student citizenship status.

As a Rowland Unified employee who stood in the rain side by side with my coworkers, fighting for a fair deal, I plan to ensure we're giving staff livable wages, fair benefits, and a life of dignity through our union contracts.

These proposals address the greatest barrier facing many students: access. Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, and every family deserves a school district that listens, responds, and delivers.
I am running because I want to bring learning for all and a government that delivers to RUSD.

text: Occupation: RUSD Governing Board President
My name is Cary C. Chen, and I am running for re-election to the Rowland Unified School District Board of Education. It has been an honor to serve this community for the past sixteen years.

As a first-generation immigrant from Taiwan, I am proud to share the journey of how I established my roots in this community–finding stability, building a career, raising my family, and giving back. My path began with two years of military service as a second lieutenant officer in the Taiwan Marine Corps. I then moved to the United States to attend the University of Akron in Ohio, where I earned a Master of Science degree in Earth Science with an emphasis in Geophysics. During my graduate studies, I gained valuable classroom experience teaching physical and historical geology labs to undergraduate students.

In 1981, an opportunity to work for UNOCAL, a major California-based oil company, allowed me to settle my family in the RUSD community. All of my children were educated within RUSD, achieved their goals, and are now thriving in their careers and raising families of their own.

For over sixteen years, serving our community on the RUSD Board of Education has been a deeply meaningful commitment. Since 2009, I have worked as a dedicated parent, volunteer, and trustee, including serving four terms as Board President. My leadership extends across our community, having served on the Joint Board of La Puente Valley ROP (2015–2016), as President of the Rowland Heights Buckboard Days Parade Committee (2015), and as President of the Rowland Heights Community Coordinating Council (2022–2024).

As the longest-serving member of the board, my priority has always been the success, safety, and well-being of our students and families. Whether drawing on my background as a geophysicist, a classroom instructor, or a local business founder, my focus remains entirely on ensuring our schools provide a high-quality education that prepares every student for a bright future. I would be honored to earn your vote to continue this vital work.
